customManagers.description: Testcontainers images are plain string literals in TypeScript, so no built-in manager reads them. The file list is explicit: a new file that boots a container has to be added here.
The manually invoked Alertmanager live test pins its three images as module constants.
BuildKit is a pipeline variable rather than an image key, so the gitlabci manager does not see it.
The manually invoked Argo CD live test pins its kind node image as a shell variable, and no built-in manager reads shell scripts.

packageRules.description: The Argo CD live test runs a hand-pinned ARGOCD_VERSION that no manager reads, and Argo CD 3.4 is tested only up to Kubernetes 1.35. Move this cap together with ARGOCD_VERSION.

Socket Mode 3 sends heartbeats through undici.ping, which Bun does not expose, so the API would lose its Slack connection. test:slack-socket-compat fails on it. Lift this cap only once that check passes on the pinned Bun.

The Claude Agent SDK inlines its own zod 4.4 core to validate MCP tool input. zod 4.5 marks a .default() field optin 'defaulted', which that core reads as required, so every terminal tool call that omits a defaulted field fails validation. The agent-sdk runtime tests fail on it. Lift this cap once the Agent SDK bundles zod 4.5 or later.
Every non-major update across all managers lands in one weekly branch.

Every major update lands in one second weekly branch, kept apart from non-major so a major that needs a code or runtime migration never blocks routine bumps. The tradeoff: one broken major blocks the others until it is fixed or capped with allowedVersions. Coupled packages rely on these two groups to move together: bun across its four managers, drizzle-orm with drizzle-kit, vitest with @vitest/coverage-v8, and the MCP client with the MCP server.

A replacement swaps one package name for a different one, so it changes dependency identity rather than version, and the npm cooldown preset deliberately exempts it. Hold it behind the dashboard so review does not read it as a routine bump.

Last on purpose. packageRules apply top to bottom, so this overrides the fix type that config:recommended sets for runtime dependencies. release-please reads fix as a patch release and would publish an image for every dependency bump.
